newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Slovnaft says troubled by Czech govt moves.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Slovnaft says troubled by Czech govt moves.

text.p: Slovak oil refiner Slovnaft said on Thursday it would not allow a recently adopted Czech import deposit plan to undermine its markets in the Czech republic.
"The Czech market remains our dominant target and we will not give up our position there," Slavomir Hatina, Slovnaft's general director told Reuters.
Last week, the Czech cabinet unveiled a package of measures aimed at revitalising economic growth and eliminating budget and current account deficits.
Under the scheme, importers will be required to deposit 20 percent of the value of imported goods on an interest-free account for 180 days.

Hatina said the measure will negatively effect Slovnaft's exports of motor fuels, heating oils and lubricants to the Czech Republic, which totalled 6.8 billion crowns, or 38.8 percent of its overall exports in 1996.
"We have already taken the neccessary and serious moves to ensure the maintenance of the continuous flow of our products to Czechs," Hatina said.
He declined to give details on the moves, but hinted the situation would force the company to revise its business plans for 1997.
"It is logical that this will cost something," he said. "We must seek other opportunities in our business plan to save the money to cure this problem."
Besides exports, Slovnaft runs 12 filling stations in the Czech Republic. In 1995, Slovnaft purchased a 51-percent stake in Benzinol, which runs another five petrol stations in the Czech Republic.
